results.evidence: The set-eligibility command is registered in cottonwood/cli.py. Its code path in cottonwood/eligibility.py sets eligibility and source_url on the contact. It inserts one activity with type eligibility_set, contact_id set, lead_id NULL and payload json.dumps({from, to, basis}). The basis is public-source-url when the new value is eligible. The success line is 'contact N: eligibility unknown -> eligible', and the command exits 0 (EXIT_OK). The eligibility checks (name, email, no other not-deleted contact with the same email_norm, not suppressed) all pass for the AC's contact. tests/test_set_eligibility.py asserts exactly this scenario through main(): exit code, printed line, stored eligibility and source_url, one activity, lead_id None, and the payload dict. All 21 tests in that file pass. I could not run the CLI by hand because the read-only policy blocked my script. The payload check compares parsed JSON, so key order and spacing are not checked.

I ran tests/test_set_eligibility.py and all 21 tests passed. test_eligible_without_source_url_is_refused calls set-eligibility with 'eligible' and no --source-url. It asserts exit 1 (EXIT_REFUSED = 1, cli.py:31) and stderr exactly ['error: source-url: required']. test_eligible_with_a_bad_source_url_is_refused covers ftp://acme.example/x and asserts exit 1 and exactly 'error: source-url: url'. Both tests then call _unchanged, which asserts the contact is still unknown with source_url NULL and that the activities table is empty. The _unchanged check covers only the eligibility and source_url fields of that one contact, not every contact column. The CLI prints one 'error: {field}: {rule}' line per failure (_run_set_eligibility in cottonwood/cli.py, the EligibilityError handler).

results.evidence: In cottonwood/eligibility.py, _failures() adds ('contact','suppressed') for 'eligible' and for 'unknown' when the email_norm is in suppression. The CLI prints each failure as 'error: contact: suppressed' and returns EXIT_REFUSED. 'ineligible' has no suppression check, so it succeeds. It writes an eligibility_set activity with basis 'manual', because the payload basis is 'public-source-url' only when to == ELIGIBLE. tests/test_set_eligibility.py (lines 162-196) covers all three cases: the eligible and unknown refusals with exact stderr, and ineligible exiting 0 with payload {from: unknown, to: ineligible, basis: manual}. All 24 tests in the file pass. I did not run the CLI by hand outside the tests.

results.evidence: eligibility._failures appends (contact, deleted) when deleted_at is set and (contact, identity) when name or email is missing or email_norm is shared with another not-deleted contact. It also appends (contact, suppressed) for a suppressed address, so a suppressed and nameless contact gets both lines. cli._run_set_eligibility prints 'error: field: rule' for each failure and returns EXIT_REFUSED, which is 1 (cli.py:31). tests/test_set_eligibility.py covers deleted, nameless, whitespace-name, no-email, shared-email and the combined suppressed+nameless case. I did not run the CLI by hand. All 21 tests in that file pass. The combined-case test also expects 'error: source-url: required', because it omits --source-url, so no test sets suppressed and nameless together with a source URL.

ContactNotFound renders 'no contact 99'; the CLI prints 'error: no contact 99' to stderr and returns EXIT_REFUSED, which is 1 (cli.py:31). When the value is unchanged, _apply returns activity_id=None with no UPDATE or INSERT, and line() prints 'contact 1: eligibility already eligible'; the CLI exits 0. tests/test_set_eligibility.py::test_unknown_contact_id_is_refused and ::test_setting_the_current_value_is_a_no_op cover both cases, including that no activities are written. All 24 tests in that file pass. One caveat: the checks run before the no-op test, so a suppressed or ambiguous contact that already holds the value is refused instead. That is outside this AC's scenario.
